characters.continuity: Marvel Comics (Earth-616), Weapon X, Marvel Comics Presents #72-84 (1991)
characters.summary: Logan during the Weapon X program: kidnapped, mind-wiped and bonded with adamantium, then used as a near-mindless feral killer with adamantium claws and a healing factor until he breaks loose and escapes into the Canadian wilderness.

mechanisms: Healing factor (wounds heal; shrugs off the drugs pumped into him)

weaknesses: His mind is wiped and controlled by the Weapon X staff through chemical and mechanical conditioning; for most of the story he is in a near-mindless state
mobility: Not established beyond human-level running and climbing
limitations: No ranged attack: fights with claws only
Acts on conditioning and instinct rather than strategy while under Weapon X control
characters.formDifferences: The roster form is the 1991 Weapon X storyline, not the MCU film Wolverine: freshly adamantium-bonded, mind-wiped and largely feral, without his later X-Men experience or costume.

sources.supports: Plot of Weapon X: the Professor, Cornelius and Hines wipe Logan's mind and bond adamantium to his bones to make a killing machine; adamantium-coated claws; he kills the soldiers at the wilderness site except Malcolm Colcord and escapes into the wilderness.

Weapon X (1991) details: he is forced to kill a pack of wolves and to fight and behead a grizzly bear; his wounds heal and he fights off the drugs; the mind control is chemical/mechanical; he goes into a frenzy, kills staff and escapes into the snow.
Review of Marvel Comics Presents #72-84: Logan was kidnapped and forced into the experiment; the adamantium infusion makes his claws pop out; he goes feral, stalking and killing doctors and soldiers.

feats.claim: Forced by the Professor to kill a pack of feral wolves.
Fought and beheaded a grizzly bear.
Broke loose, stalked and killed the doctors and soldiers of the facility one by one.

notableResults.note: Killed it in a forced test.
Killed the soldiers at the wilderness site except Malcolm Colcord and escaped; the Professor, Cornelius and Hines survived behind a secured room he could not break into.

unknowns: How far his healing factor extends in this storyline (no specific injury-recovery feat beyond healed wounds is documented in the sources).

campaignTags.claim: Healing factor shown: his wounds heal and he fights off the drugs pumped into him.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Doctor Strange 2016 through Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness 2022)
characters.summary: Wong is a Kamar-Taj master who became Sorcerer Supreme during the Blip. He fights with sorcery and weaponizes Sling Ring portals, redirecting blows back at attackers and cutting enemies off.

mechanisms: Mystic protective charms (gave Strange the Guardian Vishanti charm in What If...?)

weaknesses: Ordinary human body: he was killed by debris fighting Kaecilius's Zealots in Hong Kong until Strange reversed time
limitations: Relies on spellcasting and portals rather than physical power; took a punch from Abomination before turning the fight

sources.supports: MCU Wong: beat Abomination with a Sling Ring portal that made him knock himself out; sent Cull Obsidian to Antarctica through a portal and severed his arm; led sorcerers in Endgame's final battle; trapped Wanda in an energy prism; became Sorcerer Supreme during the Blip; killed by debris fighting the Zealots.

feats.claim: Led his own team of sorcerers in the final battle against Thanos's army.
Trapped Wanda Maximoff in an energy prism with the Souls of the Damned during the final battle.
feats.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Cage match: after taking a punch, opened a Sling Ring portal that made Abomination knock himself out.
Sent him through a portal to Antarctica and severed his arm by closing it.
Killed by debris defending the Hong Kong Sanctum; restored when Strange reversed time.

campaignTags.claim: Sorcerer Supreme of Kamar-Taj who fights with spells and Sling Ring portals.
Kamar-Taj sorcerer and Sorcerer Supreme who casts binding spells such as the energy prism used on Wanda.
Opens Sling Ring portals and weaponizes them (Abomination, Cull Obsidian).
Travels through his own Sling Ring portals.

unknowns: Final outcome of his stand against Wanda in Multiverse of Madness is not stated in the cited source.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
characters.summary: Xu Wenwu is a centuries-old warlord whose Ten Rings stop him ageing and serve as energy projectiles, shields and propulsion, backed by expert martial arts.

techniques: Ten Rings fired individually or together as energy projectiles

weaknesses: A fighter who masters the rings' flow can turn them against him (Ying Li redirected them; Shang-Chi took control of all ten)
limitations: His longevity depends on wearing the Ten Rings: they stop him ageing only while worn

sources.supports: Xu Wenwu: the rings stop him ageing while worn; conquered kingdoms over the millennia; ring projectiles, energy barrier and propulsion; beat Shang-Chi in their first Ta Lo fight; Ying held her own and redirected the rings; Shang-Chi later controlled all ten rings; killed by the Dweller-in-Darkness.

feats.claim: Conquered kingdoms over the millennia with the Ten Rings.
feats.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

feats.claim: Launched himself into the air with the rings and knocked Shang-Chi into the lake with great force.
feats.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: First fight at Ta Lo: kicked him down and sent him into the lake.

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Rematch: Shang-Chi took control of all ten rings and then dropped them rather than kill him.

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: She held her own against the rings and redirected them, sending him into the river (their first meeting).

conditional.ability: Agelessness, ring projectiles, barrier and propulsion

campaignTags.claim: Wields the Ten Rings, which stop him ageing and fire energy projectiles.

unknowns: The origin of the Ten Rings is not explained in the film.

characters.summary: Yelena Belova is a Red Room-trained Widow and Natasha's peer in combat, using a Widow's Bite gauntlet, pistols and wrist grappling lines.
limitations: No superhuman powers; relies on training and gear

sources.supports: MCU Yelena: full Red Room skill set; Widow's Bite gauntlet delivers a bio-electric shock; Glock sidearm; wrist grappling lines; fought Natasha in Budapest then teamed with her; the Red Room assault killed Dreykov and freed the Widows; hunted Clint Barton in Hawkeye.

feats.claim: With Natasha and allies, destroyed the Red Room program, killing Dreykov and freeing the captive Widows.

notableResults.note: Budapest reunion fight; the source names no winner and they then team up.

campaignTags.claim: Widow's Bite gauntlet delivers a bio-electric shock.

unknowns: Outcome of her fight with Clint Barton in Hawkeye is not stated in the cited source.
Stealth and infiltration are described only as skills; no specific stealth feat was found, so no stealth tag (owner ruling).

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Guardians of the Galaxy 2014, Vol. 2 2017)
characters.summary: Yondu Udonta is a Ravager captain who kills with a Yaka arrow steered by whistling, and pilots Ravager M-Ships.

mechanisms: Kills attackers with the arrow before they close in

weaknesses: Needs his head fin to control the arrow: after the mutiny a prototype fin had to be fitted before he could use it again
The arrow can be broken (it broke on Ego's planet and Rocket had to reassemble it)
limitations: The arrow is steered by high-pitched whistling, which takes training

sources.supports: Yaka arrow is controlled by whistled sonic frequencies; Groot fetched Yondu's prototype fin for Rocket to attach; he slaughtered the mutinous Ravagers; on Xandar he killed Sakaaran soldiers and destroyed a Necrocraft; the arrow broke on Ego's planet.
Yondu used an M-ship to abduct Peter Quill; on Xandar his ship was damaged by a Necrocraft and he lost altitude and crashed.

feats.claim: Slaughtered the mutinous Ravagers aboard the Eclector with the Yaka arrow.
Killed surrounding Sakaaran soldiers and destroyed a Necrocraft with the arrow.

notableResults.note: Ground fight after his M-ship was shot down.

campaignTags.claim: Flew his own M-ship (abducted Quill; shot down over Xandar).

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, Thor: Love and Thunder (2022)
characters.summary: Zeus rules Omnipotence City and channels lightning through his golden Thunderbolt; his magic easily binds and transforms foes, but his durability is questionable.

techniques: Thunderbolt thrown or used as a blade

mechanisms: Not established beyond divine status; he was impaled by his own Thunderbolt

weaknesses: The Thunderbolt can pierce his own flesh: he was impaled with it and seemingly killed
limitations: His lightning appears to be channeled through, and perhaps sourced from, the Thunderbolt

sources.supports: MCU Zeus: lightning manipulation channeled through the Thunderbolt; Thunderbolt can be thrown, used as a dagger and used to teleport; easily restrained Thor's group with magic and changed Thor's armor into a toga; impaled by his own weapon and seemingly killed. No height information.

feats.claim: Easily restrained Thor and his companions with magical bonds and turned Thor's armor into a toga.

notableResults.opponent: Thor, Valkyrie, Jane Foster and Korg
notableResults.note: After first binding them, he was impaled by his own Thunderbolt and seemingly killed as they escaped with it.

unknowns: Whether the comics Zeus's broader powers (shapeshifting, weather control) apply to the MCU version is not shown.
